### research/version21/construction/check.py; RELEASE-MANIFEST.json ci_scope; .github/workflows (unchanged)

No hosted job runs the Version 21 finite checks. In this review the printed source rows, exponent lists, normalized rows, expansion, height and 74,007-byte rendering were covered by my own recomputation from the TeX, with the git blob id matching the committed text. The literal equality of the 168 unchanged source rows with the printed 195 table was covered only by statistics, nine sampled rows and reuse of the PR158 and Version 19 reviews. Registering check.py in CI would close this for later heads. It should include verify229's parent comparison and a printed-195 against printed-229 comparison.

<!-- protocol-b-note:44457437665-1-fable-N4 -->
### quartic_v21.tex lines 223-227, 337-346, 562-566

Four short steps are used without derivation at the point of use; each can be reconstructed from material already present. (a) x(Q_2)=p/q: write physical U,V,W,M=a·stored, r=b·stored, p=c·stored. Rows 155-162 give R_2·c=a²·x112/C, b=c·a·q/C and R_2=a·b·q·x112. Hence c²q²=1, and R_2>0 with x112=C·x113²/q gives c=1/q. (b) The upper duplication inequality is applied to arbitrary nontorsion points m·R_0+T. It holds for every point: x(2Q)=(x²+D)²/(4x³−4Dx) gives h(x(2Q))≤4h(x)+½·log(14.06·419.6)<4h(x)+log 77. (c) prop:generator is stated on y²=x³−(75−53s)²x. The map (x,y)→(ε⁴x,ε⁶y) with ε=1+s sends 75−53s to 3−s and x(P_0) to (57−28ρ)/8=x(2R_0); this is what yields E(K)=Z·R_0+E[2]. (d) The pole blocks match Lemma v21:five-pole-obstruction with b=q·x82 (detector 0) and b=x96·q/x91² (detectors 1, 2). The square definitions use x112=C·x113²/q≠0, which holds because x101·x113≠0 by the retained scalar rows. Adding these sentences would help; none is a condition of acceptance.

<!-- protocol-b-note:44457437665-1-fable-N5 -->
### research/version21/DEPENDENCIES.md; quartic_v21.tex lines 943-945, 992-995, 1036-1038, 1153-1155; Lemma q198:affine-lucas statement (9322-9327)

The dependency table does not name four consumed items: v15:dependencies:lem:real-progression, the compact neighbourhoods of q198bb:specialization, paragraph P14 of q214:uniform-existence, and the bounds |Δ|≤14B⁴ and J_X≤4B·e^τ of q198:residual-divisibility. The statement of q198:affine-lucas still says 'sufficiently large'; Part I relies on the threshold c≥8 from its proof. Restating the lemma with the explicit threshold would make the effective claim self-contained.

<!-- protocol-b-note:44457437665-1-fable-N6 -->
### quartic_v21.tex line 18227 (retained q214 supplement); q198:trace-height statement (9046-9047)

The retained text still says that no effective construction is asserted and that the height supplier does not make the threshold effective. Those sentences describe the 214 family and the trace-height route. Part I uses H4.1 together with the new explicit torsion-sum lemma. A pointer from these passages to Part I would avoid an apparent conflict.

### quartic_v21.tex lines 497-498, 271, 412, 1048

'Weaken 3 to 6' is unexplained; the bound holds with either constant. The letter L is used for the contact denominator 7878870169, the local logarithm constant and the progression modulus, alongside the ratios L_i. Distinct symbols would help.

### source/papers/quartic/bb_native_quartics_20261124.tex lines 76-99 and 193-195; REPAIR.md section 2

thm:bb's remark still sends the reader to [Intrinsic, Section 3] for the translation and asserts a Zariski-dense two-parameter solution set; thm:pole speaks of a 'dense nondegenerate locus required by the retained finite-algebra guard arguments'. The translation actually used is REPAIR.md section 2 (intrinsic-pole section 2, native five-coordinate witnesses), and the 175 route needs only existence because no pole coordinate is inverted. At integration the REPAIR derivation should replace the stale cross-reference and the unneeded density wording.

<!-- protocol-b-note:45915251550-1-fable-N2-no-zero-contact-u-unit -->
### source/computation/projective_contacts_20261126/README.md section 3 (lines 150-164); parent usage in manuscripts/quartic_v21.tex lines 1083-1131 and prime_selection_20261109_v12.tex lines 162-167

The new ten-point set has no contact at the reflection midpoint 0, so the coefficient list for the prime supplier no longer contains 0 and u is no longer one of the selected primes. The parent text uses 'u=p_{0,0} is prime' to get that u is a unit at every prepared prime and gcd(u,w)=1; the projective note says only that no new prime-pattern assertion is invoked. The step is short: every prepared prime l divides q_0 | w, so u = p_{j,theta} - c_{j,theta} w^2 is congruent to a selected prime modulo l and is an l-unit; a common prime of u and w would divide a selected prime, which exceeds w^2. Alternatively add the coefficient 0 to the fixed list, which the supplier permits and which only introduces an even valuation in the midpoint power. A sentence to this effect would help; the mathematics is unaffected.

<!-- protocol-b-note:45915251550-1-fable-N3-reference-norm-list -->
### source/papers/quartic/scalar_point163_179_20261120_v82.tex lines 186-190; shared_product_audit_20261119_v78.tex lines 351-353; harmonic README lines 105-107; compare manuscripts/quartic_v21.tex lines 629-635

The exceptional reference norms are listed as 41^2/64, 17^2/64, 63^2/64 and 7, whereas Version 21 lists 7, 41^2/2^6, 2^6 7^2/41^2, 3^4 7^3/17^2 and 17^2/(3^4 7). My own computation of the norms of x(P_0+T) for the four T in E[2](K) reproduces the Version 21 values (1681/64, 3136/1681, 27783/289, 289/567). Both lists are supported in {2,3,7,17,41}, so the use at 331 and at primes outside S' is unaffected, but the list should be reconciled when the note is integrated.

### PROJECT.md load-bearing map; docs/theorem-application-audit/; contribution README lines 143-148 and REPAIR.md line 21

The new external application (Bhargava-Burungale Theorem 2.3 / Theorem B through the native conics) and the new load-bearing steps (shared gate, synchronized depths, weighted effective sum, 331 anchor, projective contact constant) are not entered in the theorem-application inventory or the PROJECT.md map. The note says this is left to maintainer integration and claims no record, so this is recorded for that later step, not as a condition here.
